newsitem.title: UK: Volcano buries studio where rock legends recorded.
newsitem.headline: Volcano buries studio where rock legends recorded.

text.p: It was the stuff of rock'n'roll legend, a recording studio perched on a lush hilltop on the Caribbean island of Montserrat where Paul McCartney, John Lennon and Sting once made music.

But as the towering Soufriere Hills volcano continues to lay waste to the British territory with a toxic blend of ash and molten rock, Air Studio, a soundproof room built by former Beatles' producer George Martin, makes music no more.
Along with much of the island it lies in ruins, buried under a wasteland of lifeless ash.

Martin set up the studio in 1979 on a former cotton plantation. He had the white stone building put on ball-bearings so it could withstand tremors from the nearby volcano by floating on its foundation.
American balladeer Jimmy Buffet recorded the song "Volcano" within its walls, including the lyrics: "I don't know where I'm gonna go when the volcano blow."

To the island's 11,000 residents those words have proven prophetic. More than half of them have fled to Britain or to neighbouring islands, while others have taken refuge in tents and churches to the north.

In one of those churches teeming with homeless families, British-based rock group The Police once filmed the video for "Every Breath You Take". A second church they used has been completely destroyed.
Volcanologists now warn that Soufriere is on the verge of a possible "cataclysmic" eruption.

The British government has ordered the immediate evacuation of all remaining residents wishing to leave the tropical hideaway that once played host to the Rolling Stones, Simply Red, Eric Clapton and Elton John.
McCartney and Stevie Wonder recorded their duet "Ebony and Ivory", The Police made the album "Synchronicity" and Dire Straits put down "Brothers in Arms" at Martin's paradise retreat.
Elton John reportedly proposed there to his wife, a sound engineer at the studio.

Along with the rest of Montserrat, Air Studio was heavily damaged by Hurricane Hugo, which swept across the island in 1989. When the Soufriere volcano first exploded into action in 1995, the studio was destroyed. Its remains now lie in a "no access zone" because of its proximity to the active volcano.

Some of those performers who once holidayed and recorded on the island have agreed to play for free at a benefit concert in London organised by Martin, who also has a luxury home near the former Air Studio.
Eric Clapton, Elton John, Dire Straits' Mark Knopfler, Paul McCartney and Sting will play "unplugged" at the Royal Albert Hall on September 15.

"Montserrat and its people mean a great deal to me," Martin said in a statement. "For two years I have seen them suffer and live in appalling conditions...I contacted many of the great artists who had recorded there and I am deeply touched by their ready response to help and perform."
All 4,500 tickets for the event, expected to raise at least 500,000 pounds ($805,000), sold out within 90 minutes. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
